image_description: An outdoor wooden staircase with a handrail system. The stairs lead up from a lower level to a porch or deck attached to a house with white siding. The railing consists of a wooden top rail, thick wooden newel posts at the ends, and thin vertical metal balusters (spindles) in between. The background shows green foliage and trees.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The railing clearly follows the incline of the stairs, creating a distinct diagonal line from bottom-left to top-right.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A continuous wooden handrail is visible, supported by vertical balusters that appear evenly spaced along the run.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The balusters are thin, dark, vertical rods (likely metal), significantly narrower than the handrail and newel posts, fitting the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top rail appears to be a smooth, rounded wooden strip that runs parallel to the angle of the steps.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are distinct, thicker wooden posts at the bottom and top of the railing section that anchor the handrail.
The entire railing structure is aligned with the slope of the staircase.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays a mix of materials: stained wood for the handrail/newels and sleek, minimal metal rods for the balusters.
Visual textures confirm wood grain on the rails/posts and metallic sheen/smoothness on the balusters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Evenly spaced vertical posts creating rhythmic pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical balusters create a consistent, rhythmic visual pattern along the length of the stairs.

focus_areas: Connection points between balusters and handrail/treads
Consistency of baluster spacing and thickness
Shadow alignment of railing onto steps and wall

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the base of the balusters. In AI images, thin vertical lines often merge into the background or the step surface. Verify if each baluster has a distinct termination point on the stair tread. Also, check the shadow cast by the handrail; it should be sharp and consistent with the light source direction.
